newsitem.title: ITALY: EMU must be realistic on Euro economies - Italy PDS.
newsitem.headline: EMU must be realistic on Euro economies - Italy PDS.

text.p: The main party in Italy's centre-left government said on Thursday Rome was not rejoicing at Germany's gold plan row and called for a review of the real state of European economies in the drive to currency union.
"Italy does not rejoice at the German difficulties," Umberto Ranieri, foreign affairs spokesman for the Democratic Party of the Left, said in a statement.

"Our country does not hope for and is not working for a delay in the euro. It was pretty clear that the majority of countries, Germany included, had not yet finished the work of cleaning up state finances.

"In any case, what is important is to return to the interpretation of the criteria in the spirit and to the letter of the Maastricht Treaty, which speaks of a review of the conditions for entry into the euro, taking account of the prevailing medium-term economic and financial trends...and stopping this complete fixation with decimal points," he said.
His remarks referred to the 3.0 percent ratio of deficit to gross domestic product set down by the Maastricht Treaty as a condition for entry into economic and monetary union (EMU).
A single European currency, to be known as the euro, is scheduled for launch in 1999.

Pro-EMU Italy is struggling to reach the 3.0 percent goal to qualify from the start and some estimates, including forecasts by the European Commission, have suggested it will overshoot the mark by several percentage points.

Germany on Wednesday incurred the wrath of its powerful independent Bundesbank over a plan by the Bonn government to revalue gold reserves and use cash raised as a result to help meet the strict Maastricht criteria goals.

It was the strongest indication that Germany faces a real prospect of not making the grade, raising the prospect of delay to EMU's launch or a weaker single currency with more countries -- such as Italy -- in at the start.
